item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Which shows 2/3 of the square shaded?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Square divided horizontally into six equal strips with the top two strips shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle at the bottom and shaded regions above]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three strips with the two narrow outer strips shaded]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Square with an unshaded triangle spanning from the bottom edge to the top center and two shaded triangles on the sides]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Square divided vertically into three equal strips with the two outer strips shaded]

item.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which picture shows that 2/5 is equivalent to 4/10 ?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 4 squares shaded]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 2 squares shaded]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: 2-by-5 grid with 5 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle with 2 solid circles and 3 open circles]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four labeled options (A, B, C, D):
- Option A shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The two squares in the first column and the two squares in the fifth column are completely shaded black (4 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option B shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The top-left square (row 1, column 1) and bottom-right square (row 2, column 5) are shaded black (2 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option C shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. In the top row, the 1st, 3rd, and 5th squares are shaded black; in the bottom row, the 2nd and 4th squares are shaded black (5 of 10 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern).
- Option D shows a rectangular box containing five small circles scattered inside: two circles are solid black and three circles are open white circles with a black outline.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Triangular prism]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles connected in a V-shape by two triangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles and two triangles on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles and three triangles]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles, one triangle on the top right and one triangle on the bottom left]

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

options.label: B

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Circle with shaded sector]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Circle with shaded sector]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Circle with shaded sector]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Circle with shaded sector]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Circle with shaded sector]

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Large right triangle divided into smaller triangles]

In the figure above, each of the smaller triangles has the same area. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area?
reference_items.figure_description:
A large right triangle with its vertical leg on the left and horizontal leg at the bottom, divided into smaller congruent right triangles arranged in 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns:
- Row 4 (top): Column 1 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its right angle at the bottom-left and its hypotenuse along the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
- Row 3: Column 1 contains a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 2 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 2: Columns 1 and 2 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 3 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 1 (bottom): Columns 1, 2, and 3 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 4 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A half-turn about point P in the plane is applied to the shaded figure.

[Image: Shaded figure on dashed axes]

Which of the following shows the results of the half-turn?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with rightmost vertex at point P]

reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem diagram, a horizontal dashed line and a vertical dashed line intersect perpendicularly at point P, which is marked with a black dot and labeled P below the horizontal line. A shaded right triangle lies above the horizontal dashed line. Its bottom horizontal base lies along the horizontal dashed line, extending both to the left and to the right of point P, with the segment to the left of P being longer than the segment to the right of P. The right edge of the triangle is vertical, extending upward from the horizontal line. The hypotenuse connects the top-right vertex to the leftmost vertex on the horizontal dashed line. The vertical dashed line passes through the shaded triangle.

Option A shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the right.
Option B shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the left of P), its vertical side on the right extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the left.
Option C shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line, vertical side on the right extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the left.
Option D shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the right.
Option E shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line located entirely to the left of point P, touching point P at its rightmost acute vertex, with its vertical side on the left extending downward.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
